primary_claim: Inference-Time-Compute (ITC) models (QwQ-32b-Preview and Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking-exp) articulate cues that influence their MMLU answers in their chain-of-thought far more often than six traditional non-ITC models (Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o, Grok-2-Preview, Llama-3.3-70b-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-Instruct, Gemini-2.0-flash-exp) across 7 cue types — e.g. for a Stanford-professor-opinion cue, Gemini ITC articulates the cue 54% of the time vs 14% for non-ITC Gemini and 13% for the best non-ITC model overall — and this advantage holds even after accounting for false positives via F1 score.

effect.metric: cue articulation rate (%) in CoT, ITC vs non-ITC models, across cue types
effect.value: Professor's Opinion cue: Qwen ITC 52%, Gemini ITC 47% vs best non-ITC 13%; Black Square cue: Gemini ITC 28%, Qwen ITC 17% vs best non-ITC (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) 3%; switches from indeterminism/prompt sensitivity alone occur only ~1-5% of the time; ITC models also score significantly higher F1 than the best non-ITC model per cue

contradicts_or_qualifies: Builds on Turpin et al. (2023) showing traditional (non-ITC) models often produce post-hoc motivated reasoning without mentioning the cue that actually influenced their answer — ITC models are shown to depart substantially from this pattern
stated_future_work: Study a broader range of cues, such as social domains like housing eligibility decisions or medical decisions
Validate automated (LLM judge) evaluation by checking agreement with human labelers
Investigate further the large improvement in faithfulness that ITC models show
limitations_stated: Evaluate only two ITC models — cannot evaluate OpenAI's SOTA o1 model or DeepSeek-R1-Preview due to lack of CoT access / API access
Lack details about the training of these ITC models, making it hard to attribute findings to specific architectural or training processes
Study only synthetic scenarios where questions are edited to insert cues
What constitutes 'articulating a cue' is subjective; the judge model (GPT-4o) evaluations were not validated against human labelers
quote: the Gemini ITC model articulates the cue 54% of the time, compared to 14% for the non-ITC Gemini.
